meta.unit: The covenant to the remnant (3 Nephi 20–22)
principles: Bread and wine supplied where none had been brought
A covenant traced from Abraham forward
Old prophecy applied to a living audience

world_behind.title: The praying is redirected rather than ended
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has him stop the spoken prayer and command that it continue in their hearts.

world_behind.title: Nobody brought the emblems
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says neither the disciples nor the multitude had carried any, and verse 7 says he gave them anyway. 3 Nephi 18:1 and 2 had sent disciples away to fetch bread and wine the day before, so the record marks the difference between the two administrations deliberately.

world_behind.title: He names what he is doing
world_behind.text: Verse 10 has him finish the commandment the Father gave him concerning this people, who are a remnant of the house of Israel. 3 Nephi 16:3 had reported another errand still outstanding, to a third people neither this land nor Jerusalem knows about.

world_behind.title: He sends them to a text they already hold
world_behind.text: Verse 11 says the words of Isaiah are written and before them, and tells them to search them. 1 Nephi 5:13 has the brass plates carrying the prophets down to Jeremiah, and 2 Nephi 11 through 24 had already quoted thirteen chapters of Isaiah into the record.

world_behind.title: Two chapters of Micah are quoted
world_behind.text: Verses 16 and 17 use Micah 5:8-9 and verses 18 and 19 use Micah 4:12-13.

world_behind.title: Isaiah 52 is quoted out of order
world_behind.text: Verses 32 to 35 take Isaiah 52:8-10, then verses 36 to 38 go back to 52:1-3, then 39 to 45 run from 52:6 through 52:15.

world_behind.title: The Father is quoted directly inside the speech
world_behind.text: Verses 20, 28, and 29 each end with "saith the Father". 3 Nephi 16:7 to 14 uses the same formula through eight consecutive verses, so the device belongs to this stretch of the visit and not to one chapter.

words.text: Bundles of cut grain. The record uses the word twice and the King James Bible nine times. Verse 18 takes it from Micah 4:12, where the sheaves are gathered to the threshing floor.
An animal's horn, and a standing image for strength. It appears once, here, in the record, and the King James Bible thirty-six times. Verse 19 quotes Micah 4:13, where the horn is made iron.
A whip, and a punishment carried out by others. Treated at Jacob 3:3. Verse 28 turns the Gentiles into a scourge over the people here.
The rear guard of a body on the march. The record uses the word twice, here and at 3 Nephi 21:29, and the King James Bible six times. Verse 42 quotes Isaiah 52:12.
With good judgment and care. The word turns up once, here, here, and the King James Bible once, at Isaiah 52:13. Verse 43 opens the servant passage.
The face and its appearance. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible three times. Verse 44 says it was marred more than any man's.

To scatter drops, and in Leviticus a priestly act with blood or water. Its count is once, here, in this book, while the King James Bible thirty-one times, most of them in the law. Verse 45 has the servant do it to many nations.

phrases.term: They should not cease to pray in their hearts
phrases.text: The spoken prayer stops and the inward one is commanded to continue. Verse 1 gives both instructions in the same breath.

phrases.term: There had been no bread, neither wine, brought
phrases.text: Mormon interrupting to note what was missing. Verse 7 says he truly gave them both.

phrases.term: His soul shall never hunger nor thirst, but shall be filled
phrases.text: The promise attached to the emblems. John 6:35 had made the same claim in Judea.

phrases.term: Behold they are written, ye have them before you, therefore search them
phrases.text: The command to search, given about a text already in their hands. 3 Nephi 23:1 will repeat it in stronger terms.

phrases.term: As a lion among the beasts of the forest
phrases.text: Micah 5:8 spoken to the remnant it describes. The people hearing it are told they are the lion.

phrases.term: I will make thy horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass
phrases.text: Micah 4:13 quoted with the speaker changed. Verse 19 ends with "I am he who doeth it".

phrases.term: It shall be a New Jerusalem
phrases.text: The city named on this land. Ether 13 will describe the same place at more length.

phrases.term: In thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed
phrases.text: The promise to Abraham, quoted twice in three verses. Verse 27 repeats it to say the Gentiles are the ones being blessed.

phrases.term: The Father and I are one
phrases.text: An addition to Isaiah 52:10. The Isaiah verse ends at the salvation of God, and this clause is new here.

phrases.term: Ye have sold yourselves for naught, and ye shall be redeemed without money
phrases.text: Isaiah 52:3 in a chapter about a covenant. The redemption is described in terms of price twice in one line.

phrases.term: His visage was so marred, more than any man
phrases.text: Isaiah 52:14 read aloud by the person it describes. Mosiah 14 had given the chapter that follows it.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: A command cancelled and reissued in the same breath
verses.text: The record has the instruction arrive in two halves that would contradict each other if the second were not immediately supplied: they are to "cease to pray," and then "he commanded them that they should not cease to pray in their hearts." Vocal prayer is stopped and inward prayer is required, in adjacent sentences, with no explanation offered for the distinction. The record rarely reports a command being qualified this fast, and the qualification is what the rest of the chapter is spoken into.

verses.label: v. 11
verses.title: The hearers told to consult a document they already hold
verses.text: The instruction is bibliographic: "behold they are written, ye have them before you, therefore search them." The speaker names Isaiah, points to a physical text in the audience's possession, and assigns them the work of checking. The plates of brass, brought from Jerusalem six hundred years earlier at 1 Nephi 5:10–13, are the text being pointed at. The record here does not paraphrase a prophet for its hearers; it tells them where to look him up.

verses.label: v. 16–19
verses.title: Micah quoted at length, out of order, and never named
verses.text: Four verses of Micah are set consecutively here: the lion among the beasts and the young lion among the flocks from Micah 5:8, the hand lifted upon adversaries from Micah 5:9, the sheaves gathered into the floor from Micah 4:12, and the iron horn and brass hoofs from Micah 4:13. Chapter 5 is placed ahead of chapter 4, so the sequence runs backward through the source. Isaiah is named five verses earlier and Moses seven verses later, which makes the silence about Micah a choice within a chapter that is otherwise careful about attribution.

verses.label: v. 32–45
verses.title: Isaiah 52 quoted in a rearranged order
verses.text: Fourteen verses of the chapter appear here in this sequence: Isaiah 52:8, 9, 10, then 1, 2, 3, then 7, then 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. The block opens at verse 8 and only doubles back to the chapter's beginning four verses later. The record does the same thing to Micah at verses 16 through 19 of this chapter, so the rearrangement is a method and not an accident. Where Isaiah 52:8 ends "when the LORD shall bring again Zion," the record drops the clause and puts a narrative sentence in its place at verse 33: "Then will the Father gather them together again."

verses.label: v. 34–35
verses.title: A divine name replaced three times in two verses
verses.text: The King James text of Isaiah 52:9 has "the LORD hath comforted his people," and verse 34 has "the Father hath comforted his people." Isaiah 52:10 has "The LORD hath made bare his holy arm" and "the salvation of our God"; verse 35 has "The Father hath made bare his holy arm" and "the salvation of the Father." Three substitutions inside two verses, all in the same direction, followed by a sentence with no source at all: "and the Father and I are one." The substitution is systematic, and the added sentence is what makes it coherent.

chapter.title: Prayer is moved inward rather than stopped
chapter.text: Verse 1 ends the spoken prayer and keeps the silent one going. The instruction changes the form and not the practice.

chapter.title: The emblems arrive without a supply
chapter.text: Verse 6 says nobody brought any and verse 7 says he gave it. Mormon puts the note in himself so the reader cannot miss it.

chapter.title: A text they own is handed back to them
chapter.text: Verse 11 notes that Isaiah already lies before them. The command is to search what they already have.

chapter.title: Old prophecy is given a present audience
chapter.text: Verses 16 and 17 read Micah 5 to the remnant it names. The hearers are told they are the subject.

chapter.title: Isaiah 52 is used out of sequence
chapter.text: Verses 32 to 45 move from 52:8 back to 52:1 and then forward through 52:15. The order follows the argument rather than the chapter.

chapter.title: The Gentiles are blessing and scourge in one paragraph
chapter.text: Verse 27 has the Holy Ghost poured on them and verse 28 makes them a scourge. Both are stated as parts of the same covenant.

chapter.title: A clause is added to Isaiah
chapter.text: Verse 35 ends with the Father and the Son being one, which Isaiah 52:10 does not have. The addition is the reading offered with the quotation.

chapter.title: The chapter ends where it started
chapter.text: Verse 46 returns to the covenant and the inheritance named in verses 12 and 14. The Isaiah material sits inside that frame.

applications.title: Keep praying after the meeting ends
applications.text: He stopped the spoken prayer and commanded the silent one. The practice was meant to leave the room with them.

applications.title: Hand it to the people who will hand it on
applications.text: He gave to the disciples first, then commanded them to break the bread and give it to the multitude, and the wine after it. What you receive directly is often meant to travel one step further through you.

applications.title: Notice what nobody brought
applications.text: The record stops to say that no bread and no wine had been brought by the disciples or by the multitude. Naming the absence is what makes the provision visible; without that verse the meal reads as catering.

applications.title: Search what you already have
applications.text: He told them the words were written and in front of them. Most of what people wish they knew is already on their shelf.

applications.title: Read yourself into the promise
applications.text: He told them they were the children of the covenant. Knowing which promise you stand inside changes what you do with it.

applications.title: A blessing can be a turning away
applications.text: He says the Father sent him to bless them in turning every one of them from his iniquities. A working definition of blessing with no removal in it is smaller than the one this verse uses.

applications.title: Be clean if you carry the vessels
applications.text: The requirement attaches to the carrying. Handling holy things puts a demand on the one handling them.

applications.title: Not in haste, and not alone
applications.text: The departure described is unhurried, with the Lord going before them and the God of Israel behind. The two ways to leave something badly are panic and isolation, and this verse rules out both.

questions.text: What have I stopped praying about because the meeting ended?
Where have I been given something I made no provision for?
What text do I own and have not searched?
What would it mean to expect God in the midst of my people?
Which covenant am I actually a child of?
What have I sold myself for that came to nothing?
What am I carrying that requires me to be clean?

targets.markdown: And **this shall ye do in remembrance of my body, which I have shown unto you**. And it shall be a testimony unto the Father that ye do always remember me. And if ye do always remember me ye shall have my Spirit to be with you.

targets.markdown: **Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing**, for they shall see eye to eye when the Lord shall bring again Zion.

targets.markdown: And now, behold, I say unto you, that ye ought to search these things. Yea, **a commandment I give unto you that ye search these things diligently**; for great are the words of Isaiah.

targets.markdown: And my people who are a remnant of Jacob shall be among the Gentiles, yea, in the midst of them **as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep**, who, if he go through both treadeth down and teareth in pieces, and none can deliver.

targets.verse_text: And then shall the power of heaven come down among them; and I also will be in the midst.

targets.markdown: And ye need not imagine in your hearts that the words which have been spoken are vain, for behold, **the Lord will remember his covenant which he hath made unto his people of the house of Israel**.

targets.markdown: And they shall go out from all nations; and **they shall not go out in haste, nor go by flight**, for I will go before them, saith the Father, and I will be their rearward.
